questions.question: Explain how the skeleton supports the body. Give two examples.
questions.expected_answer: Bones are hard and stiff, so they hold up the softer parts and give the body its shape. For example, the backbone keeps us upright, the leg bones carry the body's weight, and the hip bones carry the weight of the upper body to the legs.

questions.question: Name three parts of the skeleton that protect organs, and the organs they protect.
questions.expected_answer: The skull protects the brain and eyes, the backbone protects the spinal cord, and the rib cage protects the heart and lungs.

questions.question: Which bones do we use for movement, and how are other vertebrates' limbs suited to the way they move?
questions.expected_answer: We use the limb bones of the arms and legs, joined to the shoulders and the hip bones. Birds have wings for flying, penguins have flippers for swimming, frogs have long back legs for jumping, and snakes have no limbs and move with their long backbone.
